uzo.purpose: Names a page or section; its level is structure, its size is design.

instead.kialo: A bold paragraph that heads a section is a heading, because a screen reader reads the levels as the table of contents and a bold word is not in it; the titolo with its level says what the weight only shows.

boundary.kialo: A heading row with actions beside it is a pattern of the page, because the heading names the page and the actions act on it: the pagxo, whose title, badges and actions stand in that row with one primary at most.

containers.name: page-section
containers.kialo: A section of a page starts with its heading, because the heading is what a person skims and what a screen reader lists.

with.kialo: A dialog is named by its heading, because the heading says the decision it asks for; the dialog composes the titolo at level 2, its own document.
A notice may carry a heading over its message, because a heading lets a person skim what the notice is about; its heading is a text of the notice, no level of the page.
An empty state names what is missing in its text, because that sentence is what a person reads first; it is a text of the state, no level of the page.
A table is named by its caption, which stands visible above it, because the caption says what the rows are; the caption is the table's, no level of the page.
